strategy_title: Tiled In-Register Transpose for Coalesced Memory Access
strategy_description: When a kernel performs a layout permutation (e.g., NHWC→NCHW) with stride-N loads where N>>1, consecutive threads access addresses far apart, causing 0% L1 hit rate and near-100% L2 throughput. Replacing the direct uncoalesced load→store with a tiled transpose—loading a 2D tile coalesced along the stride-1 source axis, transposing in-register via tl.trans(), then storing coalesced along the stride-1 destination axis—converts stride-N accesses to stride-1, dramatically reducing L2 pressure (96.85%→58.99%) and L1TEX stall cycles (75.3→39.68 cycles/instruction). This pattern applies to any pure data-movement kernel where the load and store access patterns have orthogonal stride-1 dimensions.
slow_pseudocode:
# Uncoalesced: threads vary along spatial axis, but source stride along spatial = 128 (uncoalesced)
@triton.jit
def kernel(in_ptr, out_ptr, ynumel, xnumel, YBLOCK, XBLOCK):
    yindex = pid_y * YBLOCK + arange(YBLOCK)[:, None]  # channel/batch
    xindex = pid_x * XBLOCK + arange(XBLOCK)[None, :]  # spatial
    xmask = xindex < xnumel
    c = yindex % C; b = yindex // C
    # stride-C load: consecutive threads differ by C floats -> uncoalesced
    val = load(in_ptr + c + C * xindex + B_stride * b, xmask)
    store(out_ptr + xindex + X_stride * yindex, val, xmask)
fast_pseudocode:
# Coalesced tiled transpose: load along stride-1 channel axis, tl.trans(), store along stride-1 spatial axis
@triton.autotune(configs=[Config({'YBLOCK':32,'XBLOCK':32},num_warps=4,num_stages=3), ...], key=['ynumel','xnumel'])
@triton.jit
def kernel(in_ptr, out_ptr, ynumel, xnumel, YBLOCK, XBLOCK):
    bc_idx = pid_bc * YBLOCK + arange(YBLOCK)  # [YBLOCK] channel/batch
    x_idx  = pid_x  * XBLOCK + arange(XBLOCK)  # [XBLOCK] spatial
    c = bc_idx % C; b = bc_idx // C
    # stride-1 load along channel axis: coalesced
    src = c[:, None] + C * x_idx[None, :] + B_stride * b[:, None]  # [YBLOCK, XBLOCK]
    mask = (bc_idx < ynumel)[:, None] & (x_idx < xnumel)[None, :]
    tile = load(in_ptr + src, mask)           # [YBLOCK, XBLOCK]
    tile_T = tl.trans(tile)                   # [XBLOCK, YBLOCK] in-register
    # stride-1 store along spatial axis: coalesced
    dst = x_idx[:, None] + X_stride * bc_idx[None, :]  # [XBLOCK, YBLOCK]
    store(out_ptr + dst, tile_T, tl.trans(mask))
applicable_when: Kernel performs a pure layout permutation (transpose/reshape) where the load access pattern has stride >> 1 along the thread dimension; L1/TEX Hit Rate is 0% or near-0%; L2 Cache Throughput is >80%; Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction is high (>50) due to CPIStall on L1TEX; the source tensor has a stride-1 dimension orthogonal to the destination's stride-1 dimension.
do_not_apply_when: The kernel performs non-trivial arithmetic on loaded values (not pure data movement); the source and destination layouts share the same stride-1 dimension (already coalesced); TILE_C and TILE_X cannot both be powers of 2 (required by tl.trans()); the tensor dimensions are too small to amortize the tiling overhead.
framework_notes: tl.trans() in Triton requires both tile dimensions to be powers of 2 and tl.constexpr. All autotune configs must satisfy this. tl.trans() compiles to efficient register shuffles on Ampere/Hopper (SM 8.0+). The autotune key should be the logical dimension sizes (ynumel, xnumel) to allow the autotuner to select optimal tile shapes. Equivalent in CUDA would be shared-memory tiled transpose with __syncthreads().
